macro.regime: Oil-shock risk-off cracks the melt-up: Brent >$100 and year-high yields, hawkish Fed
macro.narrative: Re-verified Fri 24 Jul 07:00 SGT (pre-Asia-open) against the Thu 23 Jul US close; levels as of that close. The melt-up cracked: a Middle-East escalation — Iran-backed Houthis struck two Saudi tankers and the ceasefire collapsed — sent Brent above $100 intraday (WTI ~$90) and pushed Treasury yields to year-highs (10Y ~4.62%, 2Y ~4.26%), triggering a broad risk-off led by mega-cap tech (S&P -1.2% to 7,408, Nasdaq -2.2% to 25,138; Alphabet -7% on AI-capex worry, Tesla -14% on earnings). The oil spike revives the inflation impulse just as the 28-29 Jul FOMC (~83% hold at 3.50-3.75%, no cut priced, a live hike tail) approaches under a hawkish Chair Warsh — Goldman warns $120 Brent if the Strait of Hormuz stays disrupted. Gold slipped ~2% to ~$4,060 as higher real yields bit even amid the risk-off, while silver held ~$60 (still ~+130% YTD, gold ~+70%); the metals are now trading as rate/geopolitical assets, not clean hedges, into the Fed. Credit shows no stress (HY OAS ~268bp) and longer-term breadth stayed broad (~69% of the S&P above its 200-DMA going into the selloff), so this reads as a sharp oil/rate-driven narrowing rather than a break — but Fear-reading sentiment (CNN Fear&Greed ~43, crypto 31) and the hawkish Fed leave the tape vulnerable. The single biggest cross-book driver remains the Hormuz war premium: bullish oil, mixed for metals via real rates, hawkish for the Fed (a headwind for HK tech, S-REITs and levered silver). Watch: the 29 Jul FOMC, the end-July MAS review after Singapore core CPI accelerated to 1.6%, and any Hormuz de-escalation.
